assertions.description: The declarative entry-types vocabulary maps onto real timeline types: "navigation" is a supported performance entry type.
"mark" — the type include-user-timing forwards — is a supported performance entry type.
"visibility-state" — in Chromium's declarative vocabulary — is a supported performance entry type.
"largest-contentful-paint" — in Chromium's declarative vocabulary — is a supported performance entry type.
performance.mark carries an arbitrary detail payload — the channel the report format forwards verbatim for allowlisted marks.
assertions.test: (() => { const m = performance.mark("dpo-conformance-detail-probe", { detail: { ok: 1 } }); const good = !!m && !!m.detail && m.detail.ok === 1; performance.clearMarks("dpo-conformance-detail-probe"); return good; })()

assertions.description: Visibility timeline entries are named exactly "visible" or "hidden" — the names Chromium's implementation writes into the report's visibility-state entries.
assertions.test: (() => { const v = performance.getEntriesByType("visibility-state"); return v.length > 0 && v.every((e) => e.name === "visible" || e.name === "hidden"); })()

assertions.description: Activation is header-only by design: no "session-end" entry type in the JS timeline and no PerformanceSessionEndTiming global — the terminal entry exists only inside the POSTed report.

A navigation response carrying Performance-Observer plus Reporting-Endpoints causes the browser to POST an application/reports+json report of type "performance-observer" (ending with the session-end-event entry) at session termination.
assertions.test: Requires a server sending the Performance-Observer + Reporting-Endpoints header pair on the main-document navigation with the DeclarativePerformanceObserver flag or origin-trial token active, and an endpoint to receive the report at tab close / navigation away / BFCache entry / renderer crash. None of that is observable from page JavaScript on this deployment.
